component.name: Voicemod Linux
component.summary: Native clean-room voice changer for Linux

description.p: A from-scratch, open-source (MIT/Apache-2.0) reimplementation of the voice-changer concept for Linux: real-time DSP voice effects, a multi-format soundboard and a real PipeWire virtual microphone — no Windows drivers, no proprietary code.

The headless daemon (vm-daemon) owns the real-time audio pipeline; the native interface (vm-ui) drives it over a local WebSocket Control API that third-party tools (e.g. Stream Deck plugins) can also use.

Routing and UX cycle: per-application passthrough into the soundboard bus, 30-second Instant Replay with WAV export, a first-run setup wizard, an interactive graphic EQ, monitor mix and sidechain ducking, an OBS WebSocket bridge, MIDI learn, neural denoisers, autogain, autotune and an IR convolver, plus per-device voice profiles and a complete CLI for the Control API.

Usability, performance and integration cycle: RT health dashboard with watchdog, global hotkeys with push-to-talk/mute, Stream Deck / Companion surface, saved noise profiles with instant warmup, low-latency STFT switch, five factory persona voices, and login autostart with a system tray.
Ready-to-use factory mic preset (mic-npr-voice) seeded on first boot: noise reduction, gate, 5-band EQ, compressor, de-esser and limiter, with new real-time DSP nodes for each stage.
First public release: real-time DSP voice effects, multi-format soundboard and a real PipeWire virtual microphone, with a native egui client and a WebSocket Control API for third-party tools.
